gap_rationale:
I searched brain-retraining and long-COVID/ME program listings, Reddit and podcast mentions, and trial registries, and checked candidates against the reviewed and excluded lists. The main gaps are not more commercial courses, since the main ones are covered and newer ones such as Emptying the Bucket, Suzy Bolt and Healing Space are low-prominence or already excluded. The gaps are mainstream or academic programs a scholarly survey would be expected to cover, and that the commercial programs define themselves against.
(1) CBT/GET for CFS (PACE), the historical guideline-endorsed precursor and center of the controversy.
(2) Aarhus STreSS / bodily distress syndrome, the clearest academic 'one mechanism across all functional syndromes' program.
(3) IFS, highly prominent in current mind-body pain communities.
(4) Physio4FMD, the mainstream FND rehabilitation protocol with a 2024 Lancet Neurology RCT.
(5) Wise-Anderson Protocol, the main named program for pelvic pain, which otherwise has no coverage.
(6) ENO Breathe, an NHS-adopted long-COVID mind-body RCT.
(7) FibroGuide/PainGuide, from the Clauw group behind the nociplastic/centralized-pain construct.
(8) DARE / Claire Weekes, a root of brain-retraining and a popular anxiety app.
(9) Mayo-style interdisciplinary pain rehabilitation, the insurance-reimbursed mainstream comparator with Fordyce roots.
(10) The Center for Mind-Body Medicine, a long-standing program in the same spirit.
Considered but not added: Brainspotting, Havening, the Perrin Technique, myofascial release (John Barnes), Neuro Emotional Technique, chiropractic functional neurology, psychedelic/ketamine therapy, and hypnosis for pain (Jensen). They were left out for lower prominence, mechanisms outside scope, or overlap with existing entries.
Some URLs need verification: the PACE page, pelvicpainhelp.com, the ENO Breathe page, painguide.com and the Mayo page.
